visual_action: A montage of scenic, picturesque B-roll shots of various U.S. National Parks. The video shows Zion National Park at night with a starry sky, a waterfall in the Grand Canyon as seen from inside a cave, a lone Joshua Tree at sunset, and a wide landscape of Denali National Park with forests and mountains in autumn colors.

cast.name: Donald Trump
cast.evidence: The text 'trump wants to drill on our national parks for oil' is overlaid on all the video clips.

cast.name: Democratic Party
cast.evidence: The video was posted by the official @democrats account.

on_screen_text.text: trump wants to drill on our national parks for oil

spoken_summary: The audio consists entirely of a song with the lyrics, "How much sorrow can I take, blackbird on my shoulder, and what difference does it make, when this love is over?"
audio_music: A gentle, melancholic acoustic song ('Mystery of Love' by Sufjan Stevens) plays throughout the video. Its sad and sorrowful tone is juxtaposed with the beautiful scenery to create a sense of impending loss and tragedy.
editing_pacing: The video is a slow-paced slideshow of scenic landscape shots, with simple cuts between each location.
cultural_references: The song 'Mystery of Love' by Sufjan Stevens, which is well-known from its use in the film 'Call Me by Your Name'.
central_claim: Donald Trump plans to allow oil drilling in America's national parks, which would destroy their natural beauty.
intended_effect: To make the viewer feel sad and concerned about the potential destruction of treasured natural landscapes and to generate opposition to Donald Trump.
